executiveSummary: Q3 FY26 beat plan on ARR ($48.2M, up 9% QoQ) and gross margin (78.4%) but missed new logos by nine. Enterprise drove two-thirds of net new ARR; SMB churn rose to 4.9% on price. We propose a cheaper Starter tier and a Q4 plan to rebuild the top of the funnel, and need three decisions today.

slides.slideTitle: Q3 FY26 business review: growth held and margins widened
slides.subtitle: Northwind Analytics · Executive team · October 2026
slides.visualDescription: A clean dashboard glowing on a wall screen in a glass meeting room at dusk
slides.speakerNotes:
- Thanks, everyone. This is our Q3 review.
- Short version: revenue and margin beat plan, new logos missed, and SMB churn is the number to watch.
- We'll end with three decisions we need from this group today.
slides.purpose: Opens the review and frames the headline result
slides.intent: Orient the executives and set expectations for decisions

slides.slideTitle: Four things to cover in thirty minutes
keyBullets: Headline numbers: revenue, retention, and margin
What moved: segments, pipeline, and churn
What it means: the Q4 outlook and one trade-off
Decisions: three asks for this group
slides.speakerNotes:
- Four parts.
- We'll go fast through the headline numbers, since you've seen the pre-read.
- Most of our time should go to the churn trade-off and the decisions.
slides.purpose: Orients the room on the review's structure
slides.intent: Make them expect a decision at the end

slides.slideTitle: Q3 beat plan on revenue and margin but missed on new logos
keyBullets: $48.2M: ARR, up 9% on Q2
114%: net revenue retention
78.4%: gross margin, up 2.1 points
61: new logos, 9 short of plan
$1.9M: free cash flow
2.8%: logo churn, up from 2.1%
slides.speakerNotes:
- Six numbers, four green and two red.
- ARR of $48.2M is $0.6M ahead of plan.
- Gross margin is up because the hosting migration finished in July.
- New logos and churn are the two misses, and they're related, as you'll see.
slides.purpose: Gives the full scorecard at a glance
slides.intent: Make them see the quarter was good but not clean

slides.slideTitle: ARR has grown 8–10% every quarter for a year
slides.subtitle: Annual recurring revenue, $M
keyBullets: ARR is up 42% year over year, to $48.2M
slides.speakerNotes:
- Five quarters, each between 8.6% and 10.2% growth.
- That consistency is what lets us plan hiring with confidence.
- Year over year we're up 42%.
slides.purpose: Shows the growth trend is steady
slides.intent: Make them confident the core engine is healthy

slides.slideTitle: Enterprise drove two-thirds of new ARR this quarter
slides.subtitle: Net new ARR by segment, Q3 FY26, $M
keyBullets: Enterprise added $2.7M of the $4.0M net new ARR
slides.speakerNotes:
- Enterprise added $2.7M, mostly expansions inside existing accounts.
- Mid-market was steady at $1.1M.
- SMB added just $0.2M net, because new SMB bookings were nearly cancelled out by churn.
slides.purpose: Shows where growth actually came from
slides.intent: Make them see growth is concentrated in enterprise

slides.slideTitle: Pipeline converts well once qualified, but fewer leads came in
keyBullets: Leads: 4,820, down 14% on Q2
Qualified: 1,130, 23% of leads
Proposals: 312, 28% of qualified
Closed won: 61, 20% of proposals
slides.speakerNotes:
- Conversion at every stage is at or above our benchmarks.
- The problem is the top: leads are down 14%.
- That's mostly paid search, where cost per lead doubled after the July auction changes.
- This is why new logos missed.
slides.purpose: Locates the new-logo miss at the top of the funnel
slides.intent: Make them see the miss is fixable volume, not broken selling

slides.slideTitle: SMB churn climbed to 4.9% while mid-market churn fell
slides.subtitle: Quarterly logo churn by segment, %
keyBullets: SMB churn has risen four quarters in a row
slides.speakerNotes:
- This is the chart that worries us.
- SMB churn has risen every quarter for a year, from 3.1% to 4.9%.
- Mid-market churn is falling, so this is an SMB problem, not a product problem.
- Exit interviews point to price.
slides.purpose: Isolates the one trend moving the wrong way
slides.intent: Make them feel the urgency of SMB churn

slides.slideTitle: Small customers tell us the price outgrew the value
keyBullets: We love the dashboards, but at our size the price went up faster than what we get from it.
Owner of a 12-person agency, exit interview, August 2026
slides.speakerNotes: We ran 46 exit interviews in Q3. This quote is typical. Thirty-one of the 46 named price as the main reason, and most of those were customers under 20 seats who were moved to the new Growth plan in April.
slides.purpose: Puts a human voice on the churn trend
slides.intent: Make them accept price is the root cause

slides.subtitle: Three scenarios for the end of Q4
keyBullets: Base: $52.0M ARR if enterprise closes at Q3 rates
Upside: $53.4M ARR if both Fortune 500 pilots convert
Downside: $50.6M ARR if SMB churn reaches 6%
slides.speakerNotes:
- Our base case is $52.0M, which is plan.
- Upside is $53.4M if the two Fortune 500 pilots convert in November.
- Downside is $50.6M if SMB churn keeps climbing to 6%.
- The downside is the one we can do something about now.
slides.purpose: Frames the range of outcomes for Q4
slides.intent: Make them see the downside is controllable

slides.slideTitle: A cheaper SMB tier protects retention but puts $1.2M at risk
keyBullets: Pros: cuts SMB churn by an estimated 40%; simpler packaging; wins back price-sensitive prospects
Cons: $1.2M of ARR at risk from downgrades; sales retraining in Q4; margin dilution of 0.4 points
slides.speakerNotes:
| | Starter tier | Status quo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SMB churn | Down ~40% | Rising |
| ARR at risk | $1.2M from downgrades | $2.0M from churn by Q2 |
| Margin | −0.4 pts | Flat |
slides.intent: Make them weigh the trade-off and lean toward acting

slides.slideTitle: Our Q4 plan protects SMB and rebuilds the top of the funnel
keyBullets: October: launch the Starter tier; call 400 at-risk SMB accounts; fix the renewal email flow
November: close the two Fortune 500 pilots; hire four enterprise AEs; restart paid search
December: run the partner webinar series; review churn weekly; set FY27 targets
slides.speakerNotes:
- October is about retention: the Starter tier and direct outreach.
- November is about closing and hiring.
- December rebuilds the top of the funnel with partners, which is cheaper than paid search right now.
slides.purpose: Turns the analysis into a dated plan
slides.intent: Make them confident the team has a concrete plan

slides.slideTitle: Three decisions we need from this group today
keyBullets: Approve Starter tier pricing — Maya Chen, CRO — by October 31
Release $600K for four enterprise AEs — Tom Reyes, CFO — by November 7
Add churn to the weekly exec dashboard — Priya Nair, COO — from November 3
slides.speakerNotes:
- Three asks, each with an owner and a date.
- The pricing decision is the urgent one; every week we wait costs about 15 SMB accounts.
- The AE budget is already in the FY26 plan; we're asking to release it early.
slides.purpose: Makes the specific asks with owners and dates
slides.intent: Make them commit to the three decisions now

slides.slideTitle: Growth is healthy, and retention is the work for Q4
slides.subtitle: Questions, then decisions
slides.speakerNotes:
- To sum up: the engine is healthy, enterprise is strong, and SMB churn is the fix for Q4.
- Let's take questions, then go through the three decisions.
slides.intent: Make them leave with a clear, balanced view
